elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60–90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — operates only to prevent automatic annual renewal, not as a standing convenience right; the redline assumes "terminates this Agreement for convenience pursuant to Section 4.1" without creating one.gs

Preferred: pro-rata refund of prepaid fees

offending_extra_words: No Termination Payment shall be due in respect of any termination by the Company as a result of HDI's breach or pursuant to Section 1.6.
payable by the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1
reasons: The locked fallback level is not completed: the edit fixes only the exit-fee cap (3 months' fees) and leaves the two Vendor-side fallback requirements unaddressed — there is no express statement that HDI may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term, and the existing mutual 90-day notice is a non-renewal mechanic rather than a defined convenience right.

The redline refers to termination "for convenience pursuant to Section 4.1" but Section 4.1 as drafted contains no free-standing Customer convenience right (only notice of non-renewal), so the cross-reference is a dangling trigger; a short insertion creating a Customer convenience right on 60–90 days' notice was needed.

Minimality fails: the operation rewrites the whole of 4.1(a) and expands it from 55 to 87 words (ratio 1.58), where replacing only the Net Sales formula with "the aggregate fees payable in respect of the three (3) calendar months preceding the Termination Date" would have sufficed.

The added sentence carving out termination for HDI's breach or under Section 1.6 is a new exception beyond what the fallback requires (a fee cap), and duplicates protection already available on a for-cause termination.
Unrelated commercial terms (term length, auto-renewal, notice specifying the Termination Date) are left intact, so intent is preserved apart from the dangling "for convenience" cross-reference.
